summary: The retained evidence supports biologically neutral handling of varied morphology and correctly limits biological inference to specimen-level outcomes. Short, long, wide, curved, touching, and single-slice cases remain represented without WT morphology serving as an acceptance target. The evidence does not claim a biological group effect or anatomical organ volume.

limitations: Only one specimen per group is represented in the retained biological report: audits/evidence/v571_rc5_candidate/report/report_metadata.json:5-13.

The retained evidence demonstrates software handling of morphology categories but does not independently establish biological identity for every short, fragmented-looking, or fused-looking object: audits/claims_registry.json:53-54 and :168.
Boundary censoring is present in both complete specimen QC records: audits/evidence/v571_rc5_candidate/report/02_quality_control/data/specimen_technical_qc.csv:2 and :20.
recommended_follow_up: Acquire and review at least three independent biological specimens per group before performing group-level inference: audits/evidence/v571_rc5_candidate/report/report_metadata.json:10-13.

Use manually reviewed masks or external biological validation to distinguish genuine short nuclei from unresolved fragments where that biological conclusion is required: audits/claims_registry.json:53-54 and :168.
